text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

Poland has a real chance to become a member of the European Union in the years 2002-2003 on the condition that radical economic reform continues, the European Commission said in an opinion on Poland's ability for EU accession.
A June survey by the CBOS polling institute shows that among political institutions President Aleksander Kwasniewski leads with 68 percent support of Poles, up by six percent from April.
The Economist Intelligence Unit said in a report that the co-ruling, ex-communist Democratic Left Alliace (SLD) has the best chance to win parliamentary elections due in September.
Unstable law and slow privatisation are Poland's main sticking points in a European Commission report on the economies of Central Europe.

NFI Foksal in Poland's mass privatisation programme plans to form a construction holding of its firms Jedynka Wroclaw, Mostostal Wroclaw and Instal, with Jedynka likely becoming the leader of the group. Shareholders of textile firm Wistil will decide on August 4 on a planned capital raise. The firm plans a parallel market listing on the Warsaw bourse.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
